caption: What if an immortal snail chased you? The deal: 100 crore rupees and you never age, but a snail that never dies always knows where you are, and one touch means game over. Good news: a garden snail crawls about 1 mm a second, under 4 metres an hour. It glides on a thin film of slime, pushed by ripples of muscle along its foot. Crawling nonstop, it covers about 86 m a day, so 1 km takes it about 12 days. Delhi to Mumbai is about 1,150 km as the crow flies: roughly 36 years of crawling. One flight to London, about 6,700 km, buys you over 200 years of head start, and a full lap of Earth would take it some 1,270 years. Real garden snails rest a lot: tracked UK snails covered at most about 25 m a day. Plot twist: the limpet, a sea snail, has teeth that may be the strongest natural material ever tested. Would YOU take the deal? 👇
